notes:
Customer summary: Mid-size health system (multiple hospitals + clinics). High priority on PHI controls and residency. Wants private VPC deployment or on-prem option. Key asks: BAA, KMS/HSM integration (bring-your-own-key), fine-grained audit logs retained for 7 years, SOC2 + ISO artifacts, and proof that no telemetry leaves customer region.

Sales shorthand / recent call notes:
- "can't accept telemetry out of US-East" -> insisted on regional residency for prod.
- Interested in Redwood's fallback variant routing for DR (must remain within customer VPC or dedicated private endpoints).
- POC used sample discharge summaries, summary quality good but needs hallucination guard rails.
- Legal: wants explicit contract language for data segregation and right-to-audit.
- Security: wants KMS envelope encryption model, HSM-backed CMK, and audit trails for key usage.
- PCI question: payment tokens appear in chat logs for a small subset of workflows — needs PCI scoping guidance (likely out of scope if tokens are vaulted client-side).

Quoted from CIO: "We need to treat inference as part of our regulated surface — everything that touches PHI must be auditable and owned by us."

POC notes: resource names: cassio-poC-vpc-1, had limited egress, tested tokenization pipeline. Performance: 85th pct latency 160ms for clinical summarization model variant. Cost sensitivity: moderate; willing to pay premium for strong compliance guarantees.
compliance_mapping_summary:
SOC 2: Customer requires Type II report; focus on CC6 (logical access), CC7 (system operations), CC8 (change management). Action items: provide SOC2 Type II, map runtime RBAC roles, show audit log retention policy and proof of immutable log storage.

ISO 27001: Require evidence of ISMS scope covering private deployment. Action items: share Statement of Applicability sections relevant to access control and cryptography, provide incident response SLAs and sample tabletop results.

HIPAA / BAA: Customer will process PHI in inference. Must sign BAA; ensure PHI is processed inside customer-controlled VPC or on-prem. Action items: provide BAA template, detail encryption-in-transit and at-rest (AES-256), BYOK flow for KMS/HSM, key rotation policy, and egress prevention controls. Confirm that redact/tokenize pipeline options exist and can be enforced in the ingestion layer.

PCI considerations: Only a subset of chat flows may surface payment tokens. Recommend scoping strategy: vault tokens client-side and pass only references to model; if raw PAN data could reach inference, discuss isolating those requests in a separate, PCI-scoped environment or use client-side tokenization. Action items: provide architecture options and controls to keep PCI data out of the LLM processing path.

Audit logging: Customer requires immutable audit logs for 7 years with ability to export to their SIEM (Splunk). Action items: demonstrate log export, show audit schema (actor, action, resource, timestamp, request id), retention and WORM-config support, and support for VPC-only endpoints for log evacuation.

KMS integration: BYOK mandatory. Need HSM-backed CMKs, key usage audit, and limited access for Redwood operators. Action items: document envelope encryption flow, IAM mapping, recommended KMS policies, sample CloudTrail entries for key usage, and support for on-prem HSM connectors if required.

Overall recommendation for customer: Proceed with Redwood Private (VPC) pilot with explicit guardrails: BAA sign-off, BYOK HSM integration, log export to customer SIEM, and a PCI scoping review. Provide a one-page compliance mapping and an architecture diagram for their security team next week.
